Archive item 2: Damage Assessment Report – Khejuri Coastal Shelter
Source format: Damage assessment reports

The inspection was carried out by the undersigned along with the block-level junior engineer (JE) of the respective blocks. Weather conditions during the inspection were fair, with no rainfall on the dates of site visits. All findings are recorded on the standard DEOC damage assessment format. Digital photographs of each shelter were taken and are referenced in Annexure A of this report.

**2. Damage Categories Used**

For uniformity, the team has used the following categories as per the DEOC Damage Assessment Manual (Rev. 2024):

- **Minor** – cosmetic or non-structural damage, no impact on safety or occupancy, repair within 7 days.
- **Partial** – structural damage affecting one or more building components but not threatening total collapse; shelter may be used with caution or after temporary propping; repair required within 30 days.
- **Severe** – structural damage likely to cause collapse or make the shelter unusable; immediate evacuation and detailed engineering investigation required.

**3. Summary of Shelters Assessed**

A total of nine shelters and two community halls were inspected between 10 and 20 June 2025. The following table lists the shelters in the order of inspection. Full details for each shelter are given in Section 4.

**4. Detailed Findings – Selected Shelters**

**4.1 SH-2025-014 – Digha Fishermen Community Hall (Ramnagar II)**
Inspected on 10 June 2025 at 10:30 hrs. The hall is used for storing fishing nets during the monsoon and for community meetings. Roof is of corrugated galvanised iron (CGI) sheets on steel trusses. Minor corrosion observed on the CGI sheets near the eaves. One gutter joint is leaking. Wall plaster has hairline cracks on the southern wall. No structural concern. Recommended action: apply anti-corrosive paint, replace two gutter sections, patch plaster.

**4.2 SH-2025-015 – Mandarmani Coastal Shelter (Ramnagar II)**
Inspected on 11 June 2025 at 09:15 hrs. This is a two-storey RCC frame building. The shelter was constructed in 2016 and has a capacity of 300 persons. During the inspection, the team observed significant cracking in the shear wall on the north-east corner, spalling of concrete on the first-floor beam, and tilting of the parapet. The roof slab shows water seepage marks but no visible sagging. The damage is assessed as **severe**. The shelter should not be used for cyclone evacuation until a detailed structural investigation is conducted by a chartered engineer. The DEOC has been advised to identify an alternative shelter for the coming monsoon.

**4.3 SH-2025-016 – Khejuri Coastal Shelter (Khejuri II)**
Inspected on 12 June 2025 at 11:45 hrs. The shelter is located near the Khejuri fishing harbour, approximately 500 m from the high tide line. It is a single-storey masonry building with a CGI sheet roof on timber purlins. The shelter was used as a temporary relief camp during Cyclone Amphan in 2020 and again briefly in May 2025 for a local flood.

The damage assessment report notes Khejuri Coastal Shelter roof_damage_status as partial. Record status: current. This is the current assessment, based on the inspection conducted on 12 June 2025. The team observed that the CGI sheets on the western slope of the roof have lifted at two places, likely due to wind pressure during the May 2025 storm. The timber purlin on the west side has a visible crack at its mid-span. Additionally, the wall on the western side shows a vertical crack running from the plinth to the roof level, approximately 3 mm wide. No sign of foundation settlement was observed. The shelter is considered usable for daytime activities, but for overnight cyclone evacuation, temporary propping of the western roof truss is recommended. The roof repair should be completed within 30 days.

**5. STRUCTURAL FINDINGS – DETAILED**

**5.1 Roof – CGI Sheet Cladding (Western Slope)**

Two (2) CGI sheets on the western slope have lifted at their lower edges. Lifting is most prominent at the sheet adjoining the ridge, approximately 2.5 m from the western gable end. The fixings (J-hooks) at these locations have pulled out from the timber purlin; the holes in the sheets are elongated, indicating that the sheets were not re-fixed after the May 2025 storm. The remaining sheets on this slope are in fair condition, with surface rust at the edges but no perforations.

The eastern slope was inspected from the inside; no lifting or missing sheets observed. The ridge capping is intact.

**5.2 Timber Purlin – Western Slope**

The purlin supporting the lifted sheets has a visible crack at mid-span. The crack runs vertically through the full depth of the purlin section (approx. 100 mm x 50 mm). The crack width is approximately 2 mm at the surface and does not appear to be widening under static load. The purlin is still seated on the wall plate, but the connection at the west wall has slight lateral movement when pressure is applied by hand.

**5.3 Masonry Wall – Western Side**

A vertical crack is present on the western wall, running from the plinth to the roof level. The crack width is approximately 3 mm. The crack is located roughly 1.2 m from the south-west corner of the building. The crack follows the mortar joint for most of its length, but at one point it passes through a brick, indicating that the wall has undergone some differential movement. No corresponding crack was observed on the interior face of the same wall. The wall is load-bearing and supports the western roof truss.

**5.4 Foundation**

No sign of foundation settlement was observed. The plinth beam (where visible) is free of cracks. The ground around the building is level, with no evidence of soil washout or scour near the plinth.

**5.5 General**

The building is single-storey masonry construction with CGI sheet roof on timber purlins. The shelter was used as a temporary relief camp during Cyclone Amphan in 2020 and again briefly in May 2025 for a local flood. The building is in overall fair condition for daytime use, but is not considered safe for overnight occupation during a cyclone event without temporary propping.

The District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC), Purba Medinipur, functioned continuously from 20 May 2025 in response to Cyclone Amphan and subsequent flooding in low-lying areas along NH-116B and the coastal belt. The approval covers food, drinking water, sanitation, and temporary repair costs for the period 20 May to 31 July 2025.

2.2 The District Magistrate has directed that all expenditure be booked under the head "Cyclone Amphan – Shelter Operations" and that utilisation certificates be submitted to the State Relief Commissioner's office by 5 August 2025.

documents.title: Damage Assessment Report – Khejuri Coastal Shelter
documents.content:
The inspection was carried out by the undersigned along with the block-level junior engineer (JE) of the respective blocks. Weather conditions during the inspection were fair, with no rainfall on the dates of site visits. All findings are recorded on the standard DEOC damage assessment format. Digital photographs of each shelter were taken and are referenced in Annexure A of this report.

**2. Damage Categories Used**

For uniformity, the team has used the following categories as per the DEOC Damage Assessment Manual (Rev. 2024):

- **Minor** – cosmetic or non-structural damage, no impact on safety or occupancy, repair within 7 days.
- **Partial** – structural damage affecting one or more building components but not threatening total collapse; shelter may be used with caution or after temporary propping; repair required within 30 days.
- **Severe** – structural damage likely to cause collapse or make the shelter unusable; immediate evacuation and detailed engineering investigation required.

**3. Summary of Shelters Assessed**

A total of nine shelters and two community halls were inspected between 10 and 20 June 2025. The following table lists the shelters in the order of inspection. Full details for each shelter are given in Section 4.

**4. Detailed Findings – Selected Shelters**

**4.1 SH-2025-014 – Digha Fishermen Community Hall (Ramnagar II)**
Inspected on 10 June 2025 at 10:30 hrs. The hall is used for storing fishing nets during the monsoon and for community meetings. Roof is of corrugated galvanised iron (CGI) sheets on steel trusses. Minor corrosion observed on the CGI sheets near the eaves. One gutter joint is leaking. Wall plaster has hairline cracks on the southern wall. No structural concern. Recommended action: apply anti-corrosive paint, replace two gutter sections, patch plaster.

**4.2 SH-2025-015 – Mandarmani Coastal Shelter (Ramnagar II)**
Inspected on 11 June 2025 at 09:15 hrs. This is a two-storey RCC frame building. The shelter was constructed in 2016 and has a capacity of 300 persons. During the inspection, the team observed significant cracking in the shear wall on the north-east corner, spalling of concrete on the first-floor beam, and tilting of the parapet. The roof slab shows water seepage marks but no visible sagging. The damage is assessed as **severe**. The shelter should not be used for cyclone evacuation until a detailed structural investigation is conducted by a chartered engineer. The DEOC has been advised to identify an alternative shelter for the coming monsoon.

**4.3 SH-2025-016 – Khejuri Coastal Shelter (Khejuri II)**
Inspected on 12 June 2025 at 11:45 hrs. The shelter is located near the Khejuri fishing harbour, approximately 500 m from the high tide line. It is a single-storey masonry building with a CGI sheet roof on timber purlins. The shelter was used as a temporary relief camp during Cyclone Amphan in 2020 and again briefly in May 2025 for a local flood.

The damage assessment report notes Khejuri Coastal Shelter roof_damage_status as partial. Record status: current. This is the current assessment, based on the inspection conducted on 12 June 2025. The team observed that the CGI sheets on the western slope of the roof have lifted at two places, likely due to wind pressure during the May 2025 storm. The timber purlin on the west side has a visible crack at its mid-span. Additionally, the wall on the western side shows a vertical crack running from the plinth to the roof level, approximately 3 mm wide. No sign of foundation settlement was observed. The shelter is considered usable for daytime activities, but for overnight cyclone evacuation, temporary propping of the western roof truss is recommended. The roof repair should be completed within 30 days.

**5. STRUCTURAL FINDINGS – DETAILED**

**5.1 Roof – CGI Sheet Cladding (Western Slope)**

Two (2) CGI sheets on the western slope have lifted at their lower edges. Lifting is most prominent at the sheet adjoining the ridge, approximately 2.5 m from the western gable end. The fixings (J-hooks) at these locations have pulled out from the timber purlin; the holes in the sheets are elongated, indicating that the sheets were not re-fixed after the May 2025 storm. The remaining sheets on this slope are in fair condition, with surface rust at the edges but no perforations.

The eastern slope was inspected from the inside; no lifting or missing sheets observed. The ridge capping is intact.

**5.2 Timber Purlin – Western Slope**

The purlin supporting the lifted sheets has a visible crack at mid-span. The crack runs vertically through the full depth of the purlin section (approx. 100 mm x 50 mm). The crack width is approximately 2 mm at the surface and does not appear to be widening under static load. The purlin is still seated on the wall plate, but the connection at the west wall has slight lateral movement when pressure is applied by hand.

**5.3 Masonry Wall – Western Side**

A vertical crack is present on the western wall, running from the plinth to the roof level. The crack width is approximately 3 mm. The crack is located roughly 1.2 m from the south-west corner of the building. The crack follows the mortar joint for most of its length, but at one point it passes through a brick, indicating that the wall has undergone some differential movement. No corresponding crack was observed on the interior face of the same wall. The wall is load-bearing and supports the western roof truss.

**5.4 Foundation**

No sign of foundation settlement was observed. The plinth beam (where visible) is free of cracks. The ground around the building is level, with no evidence of soil washout or scour near the plinth.

**5.5 General**

The building is single-storey masonry construction with CGI sheet roof on timber purlins. The shelter was used as a temporary relief camp during Cyclone Amphan in 2020 and again briefly in May 2025 for a local flood. The building is in overall fair condition for daytime use, but is not considered safe for overnight occupation during a cyclone event without temporary propping.
